Application Materials.content:
Please upload these supporting documents as a PDF onto the [Graduate Admission System](https://gradapp.nus.edu.sg/portal/app_manage). The total size of your uploaded documents should not exceed **10MB**. Documents not in English must be accompanied with certified copies of the English-translated version. Incomplete applications will not be considered. **Note: You do not need to mail us any documents during the application stage.** **Letters of recommendation, reference letters and referee details are not required to be submitted.**
- Your resume: Your updated resume detailing your educational background, internship and work experience (if any), achievements, etc.
- Copy of your official identification documents: Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents: a copy of your NRIC (front and back). International applicants: a copy of your passport (identification page).
- Certified copies of your transcripts/mark sheets and degree certificate: Official transcripts and attested copy of degree scroll will be required after you are offered a place in the programme. Transcript Request Forms are available via this [link](https://msgfin.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/sites/90/2022/09/Transcript-Request-Form.pdf).
- A Letter of Motivation: _Not more than 500 words_.
- GMAT/GRE scores (optional): **GMAT:** Please designate **“National University of Singapore” (GMAT Code: DRT-MK-96 MSc in Marketing Analytics and Insights)** as your score recipient. **GRE:** Please designate **“4642 – NUS Business School MSc Programmes”** as your score recipient.
- TOEFL / IELTS scores (if applicable): **IELTS:** Please upload a softcopy of your IELTS Test Report Form via the application portal. **TOEFL:** Please upload a softcopy of your TOEFL Score Report via the application portal and indicate the institution code – “0677 National University of Singapore”.
[Upload supporting documents](https://gradapp.nus.edu.sg/portal/app_manage)
If you are offered admission, official transcripts must be sent by the institution / university in a sealed envelope with its flap bearing the security seal of the institution / university directly to: MSc Programmes Office Mochtar Riady Building Level 2 15 Kent Ridge Drive Singapore 119245

Interview Requirements.content: A strong performance in the interview (conducted for shortlisted candidates only).

Application Deadlines.content:
There is only one intake in August each year for the [single-degree MSc in Marketing Analytics and Insights](https://mscmarketing.nus.edu.sg/).
The key application dates for the August 2026 intake are:
| Date | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 1 September 2025 | Application opens |
| **15 November 2025** | Cut-off date for 1st round of application; cut-off date for study award consideration |
| **15 February 2026** | **Application deadline for all applicants** |
| By June 2026 | Notification of application outcome for all applicants |
| Late July 2026 | Orientation and commencement of classes |
Applications received on or before each cut-off date will be reviewed after the respective deadline. Admission offers for the first cut-off will be issued on a rolling basis commencing in January/February and for the second cut-off commencing in March/April. Applications will only be reviewed if both the **application form is submitted** and the **application fee is paid** by the specified deadlines. Applications are valid for the immediate upcoming intake only.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **NUS MSc in Marketing Analytics and Insights programme:** A good undergraduate degree in any discipline.
- **Work Experience (Not Required):** We do not require you to have work experience for admission into the programme. Applicants with some postgraduate work experience are also welcome to apply.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
- GMAT/GRE is optional. Applicants are welcome to submit an application without a GMAT/GRE score. A strong score may enhance the application.
- Generally, a score of **700 out of 800 for the GMAT**, or the GMAT equivalent in GRE, is expected. However, as it is not mandatory, applicants are also welcome to submit an application without a GMAT/GRE score.
- Applicants with lower GPAs are encouraged to strengthen their application with a competitive GRE or GMAT score.
- For GMAT, visit the [official GMAT website](https://www.mba.com/exams/gmat). Designate “**National University of Singapore**” (**GMAT Code: DRT-MK-96, MSc in Marketing Analytics and Insights**) as the GMAT score recipient.
- For GRE, visit the [official GRE website](https://www.ets.org/gre/?WT.ac=etshome_gre_menu_180417). Designate “**4642 – NUS Business School MSc Programmes**” as the GRE score recipient.

English Proficiency Requirements.content: If English is not the native language or medium of prior undergraduate instruction: For **TOEFL**, the internet-based test score must be at least **5.0**. For **IELTS**, the overall band score must be at least **7.0**.

Program Overview.content:
**12 Months. 40 Units.** This applies to students enrolled in the single-degree [MSc in Marketing Analytics and Insights programme](https://mscmarketing.nus.edu.sg/). The programme is structured over 12 to 15 months, and students learn from distinguished faculty members with recognised expertise in their fields, alongside peers and colleagues from diverse cultures and backgrounds.
| Orientation Week | 1st Semester | 2nd Semester | 3rd Semester |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Early August | Aug – Nov | Jan – Apr | May – Jul or Aug – Nov |
| 1 Course (0 Units): Principles of Marketing | 3 Core Courses (12 Units); 2 Elective Courses (8 Units) | 2 Core Courses (8 Units); 2 Elective Courses (8 Units) | Experiential Learning (4 Units) |
Students need to take a total of four elective courses, totalling 16 units. The Experiential Learning component can be completed in Special Terms 1 and 2 (May to July) or Semester 1 (August to November) of each Academic Year. Students complete one out of two options: an Industry Internship or a Marketing Analytics Consultancy Project. Through the internship, students engage in experiential learning by analysing and solving problems faced by peers working in marketing and analytics functions in various industries. Through the Marketing Analytics Consultancy Project, students work in groups to analyse and solve marketing- and analytics-related problems faced by actual companies, resulting in a comprehensive, in-depth business proposal or solution.
Alumni comments describe the programme as covering key topics from programming and branding to consumer behaviour, providing in-depth practical skills, opportunities to work with real businesses on genuine problems, and preparation for a career in APAC through studying in Singapore. Another Class of 2024 student stated that the programme gave a deep understanding of marketing and consumer insights, with practical insights through business simulators and case studies, and access to business career office resources including daily job listings, career workshops, and one-on-one sessions with career advisors.

Curriculum.content:
**12 Months. 40 Units.** This applies to students enrolled in the single-degree [MSc in Marketing Analytics and Insights programme](https://mscmarketing.nus.edu.sg/). The programme is structured over **12 to 15 months**.
| Orientation Week | 1st Semester | 2nd Semester | 3rd Semester |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Early August | Aug – Nov | Jan – Apr | May – Jul or Aug – Nov |
| 1 Course (0 Units): Principles of Marketing | 3 Core Courses (12 Units); 2 Elective Courses (8 Units) | 2 Core Courses (8 Units); 2 Elective Courses (8 Units) | Experiential Learning (4 Units) |
Full Course = 4 units (3 hours/week, 13 week duration).
Principles of Marketing is a refresher course carrying zero (0) units and conducted as part of orientation.
Core courses include:
- Big Data in Marketing
- Consumer Insights
- Digital Marketing
- Marketing Analytics
- Marketing Analytics Visualisation and Communications
You need to take a total of four elective courses (2 courses in each semester), totalling **16 units**. The basket of elective courses may include:
- AI in Marketing
- Customer Relationship Management
- Marketing Analysis & Decision Making
- Marketing Strategy
- Personal Selling & Sales Management
- Pricing Analytics
- Product and Brand Management
- Python Programming for Marketing Analytics
- Research for Marketing Insights
The Experiential Learning component can be completed in Special Terms 1 and 2 (May to July) or Semester 1 (August to November) of each Academic Year. Students will complete one out of the two options available:
- Industry Internship
- Marketing Analytics Consultancy Project
All core and elective courses, and experiential learning options are worth **4 Units** each, unless stated otherwise. The curriculum is subject to changes. The University reserves the right to revise the curriculum.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The estimated monthly living expenses* for an international student in Singapore are outlined below:
| Expense Type | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| Accommodation | [On-campus housing](https://www.nus.edu.sg/osa/student-services/hostel-admission/graduate/hostel-options) (subject to availability) S$900 - S$1,800; Renting a room in a public housing apartment S$700 - S$1,000; Renting a room in a private apartment S$1,000 - S$2,000; Renting a 3-bedroom private apartment S$4,000 onward |
| Meals | S$300 - S$800 |
| Transport (within Singapore) | S$80 - S$200 (buses and trains) |
| Healthcare | S$52 - S$112 per consultation with a General Practitioner |
| Personal Expenses | S$200 - S$350 |

Financial Aid.content:
Limited **full scholarships** & **study awards** are available for selected outstanding applicants. Study awards will cover a portion of the programme fees. There is no need to apply separately for study awards or scholarships; however, candidates must submit an application by the [first cut-off date](https://mim.nus.edu.sg/fees-finances/awards/). Study award and scholarship recipients are chosen based on merit in the following categories:
- **Excellence**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have done exceptionally well in their academics, as well as during the application process (e.g. interviews).
- **Diversity**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who come from diverse personal and professional backgrounds and experience, and can contribute to the overall experience of their cohort.
- **Resilience**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have demonstrated determination and resilience to achieve excellence in spite of adversity and hardship.
- **Achievers**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have achievements in activities outside of the classroom, e.g. promoting or contributing to the UN SDGs; community service in social, environment, or other sectors; entrepreneurship, etc.
- **Local Candidates**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are Singaporeans or Singapore PRs.
- **ASEAN Candidates**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are nationals of an ASEAN country.
- **NUS Alumni**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are NUS Alumni.

Multiple Applications.content:
If you wish to have a choice between the single and double degree programmes, you should submit an application to both, in which case, if you are shortlisted for further review, you will be considered for both the single degree programme and the double degree programme that you have applied to.
There are several possible outcomes after the interview and consideration:
- The interview panel finds you suitable for both the single or double degree programme, you will be offered to choose which programme you wish to be admitted to.
- The interview panel finds you unsuitable for the double degree programme, but a viable candidate for the single degree programme, you will be offered a place in the single degree programme.
- The interview panel finds you unsuitable for our programmes, you will not be offered a place.
You may apply for **up to 5 programmes per admission cycle**. An application number will be assigned to you when you create a new online application for each programme. If you are successful in more than one application, you can choose to be admitted to your preferred programme.
